<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4547e76eb35a65c38002a333eb79d2bcc58421cd` — the merge of head `1d5360b3eec0a62ff96e7931e8e91aea2bcbca28` into base `5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4547e76eb35a65c38002a333eb79d2bcc58421cd && git checkout 4547e76eb35a65c38002a333eb79d2bcc58421cd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1 1d5360b3eec0a62ff96e7931e8e91aea2bcbca28 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1 && git merge --no-ff 1d5360b3eec0a62ff96e7931e8e91aea2bcbca28

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5e250a65992192bdc9b3fb3be304a2fca245b2d1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

1. **Shape.** Draft PR to `main`, `Fixes #32843`, 2 files, +160/−143 = 303 lines ≤ 3000. `check-governed-merges --pr 33169`: NOT governed (default tier holds for `packages/lint/**`). 2. **Premise.** It holds, per report 6867775461. No check of the 70 agent-written sentences against the console packs had been recorded, and ruling A (6840566887) makes that agent check the card's whole work.
3. **Review against ruling A.**

View All / Modify All Records, Read and Write scope and a policy's CHECK are edited only in the Studio permission editor, whose `studio` namespace ships `en` and `zh` only (`ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/` holds `en.ts`, `zh.ts`, `index.ts`; `perm.action.viewAll` at `en.ts:30`).    - "What the fix grants": the thread read every remedy arm in every locale against the English. The three field-mask arms and the three owner-policy remedies keep their split.
   - N2 (record 6835490406) was not added, with reasoning in the body: the sentence already says the check condition bounds what an update may write, and the mechanism stays in `hint` / `os explain`. The order left it to the dev, and the reasoning holds.
   - A term table per locale is in the PR body.
4. **Gates.**
   - 505/505 tests across 11 lint files at head, including `finding-user-text.test.ts` (no sentence is the English stand-in: each one keeps its own-language sentence around the quoted screen label).
   - `dispatch-gates --ran`: 53 families accounted for, 51 exit 0, 2 NOT MEASURED with a stated prerequisite (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, which need a full build). The diff changes string values in one module and no entry point or export; CI runs both on a full build.
   - `origin/main` was merged once.
   - Check-runs on this head were all success or skipped, 0 failure, at landing; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check success.
5. **Accepted deviations.** The changeset and report use #32843. The seat's order carried a stale sibling number (#33073) in two template lines, and the thread corrected it. That is a seat error, not a deviation by the thread.
6. **Out of scope / landing.**
   - The 67 rules without sentences (#32835): out of scope by the card.
   - Ordinary queue landing: `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` now, on the standing landing go-ahead for pm-dispatch-reviewed PRs (maintainer, 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-06). On MERGED: confirm #32843 closed, remove `pm:dispatched`.
